bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: German Wirehaired Pointer owners tracking 14-16 years lifespans still lose the mid-series booster more often than the first shot, and the unprotected gap after week 8 is where parvovirus risk concentrates for this puppy.
Use the 4-row German Wirehaired Pointer schedule as your only planning spine: 8 weeks (DA2PP / DHPP); 12 weeks (DA2PP / DHPP booster); 16 weeks (DA2PP / DHPP booster); 16 weeks (Rabies).

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Delayed German Wirehaired Pointer boosters usually need one well-timed catch-up, not a homemade double dose, because spacing rules protect the puppy and guilt math does not.

Bring prior dates for every German Wirehaired Pointer row (8, 12, 16, 16 weeks on this page’s plan) so clinics can decide whether an extra DA2PP / DHPP booster is required based on gap length and age.

faqs.question: When does the German Wirehaired Pointer core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my German Wirehaired Pointer misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.
